page: Amazon Web Services c9g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 processor running at 3.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware included with this instance type. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 34 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a multi-core stress-ng CPU score of 126,148.66 and a PassMark CPU score of 60,579.41. Memory performance is highly competitive, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 8,631.41 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 326.36 GB/sec. Database and web operations perform exceptionally well, as demonstrated by a Redis SET throughput of 180.55 million operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 174.71 GB/sec. Single-threaded decompression tasks also show top-tier performance, with bzip3 decompression reaching 17.16 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture delivers high compute density and strong multi-threaded performance per resource unit. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for workloads requiring high-speed local scratch space or hardware-accelerated machine learning. The instance is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, high-throughput web serving, distributed database operations, and multi-threaded data compression tasks.

This profile makes the c9g.16xlarge highly efficient for compute-heavy applications, web serving, and multi-threaded processing tasks that do not require local storage.
